memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now when all the kings west of the Jordan heard about these things — the kings in the hill country, in the western foothills, and along the entire coast of the Mediterranean Sea as far as Lebanon (the territory of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites) — they came together to wage war against Joshua and Israel. — Josh 9:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
News of Israel's victories at Jericho and Ai spread across the land, and the response of the Canaanite kings is telling. Rather than turning to the God whose power they had heard of, they band together to fight against Him and His people. Their fear did not lead them to repentance; it hardened into resistance. They chose to unite in opposition rather than bow in surrender.

This is a sobering picture of how the human heart often responds to God. When confronted with clear evidence of His power, some soften and turn to Him, as Rahab did. Others stiffen and organise against Him. The same reports that had melted Rahab's heart in faith now stiffened these kings into war. The difference lay not in the evidence but in the response of the heart.

We see this same pattern throughout history. There has always been opposition to God and His people, sometimes organised and powerful. Yet we need not be alarmed by it. Scripture reminds us that when "the kings of the earth rise up... against the Lord," the One enthroned in heaven is not shaken (Ps 2:2-4). No alliance of human power can overturn God's purposes.

For the believer, this is quietly reassuring. Opposition may gather, and it may look formidable. But our confidence is not in the weakness of our opponents; it is in the greatness of our God. In Christ we are promised, "In this world you will have trouble. But take heart! I have overcome the world" (John 16:33). The gathered kings could not stop God then, and no opposition can stop His purposes now.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When you encounter opposition to your faith, are you alarmed, or anchored in God?
2. Why do you think the same evidence of God softens some hearts and hardens others?
3. How does knowing God is unshaken by human opposition steady your heart today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when opposition rises against You and Your people, keep me from fear. Anchor my confidence in Your greatness, for nothing can overturn Your purposes. Amen.
